why: Values and principles vs purpose/context vs compliance, governance, provenance and scope.

options.name: Institutional values and principles for AI use
options.covers: An institution-level framework or preamble stating the purpose, scope, and principles for AI use.

options.name: Purpose and context of the policy document
options.covers: Why the document exists, what problem it addresses and its context (split from P56, which keeps values and principles).

options.name: Existing law and university policy apply to AI
options.covers: AI use must follow laws (records, privacy, IP) and existing university policies (conduct, acceptable use, branding), and violations fall under those policies. Different from P45, which treats AI like a human collaborator under integrity rules. Evidence: Amherst, Boise State, Kansas State, Arizona State, Cal State, Davidson.

options.name: Governance roles, ownership and exceptions
options.covers: Names the office, officer, council or committee that interprets, implements, monitors or enforces the AI policy, or the process for granting exceptions to it. Evidence: Purdue, Rowan, Oakland, Morehouse, Northeastern, Northwestern, Portland State, Santa Clara.

options.name: How the policy was made (body, process, sources, AI assistance)
options.covers: States the process, body or date by which the AI policy or guidance was drafted, consulted on, adopted or ratified. Evidence: New Mexico State, Rice, Northeastern, Santa Clara.

options.name: Definitions and scope of the policy
options.covers: Definitions of AI, generative AI, AI tools or agentic systems that set what a policy covers (sources: Oregon State, Howard).

AI should be transparent, explainable, and accountable, and individuals should be informed and empowered to understand, challenge, and remedy AI-based AI should be reliable, safe, and secure, and its accuracy and effectiveness should be evaluated and verified for the intended use. AI should be available broadly, and its development and implementation should consider many perspectives and experiences. AI should be used in ways that uphold academic freedom, integrity, and excellence, and that foster interdisciplinary collaboration and innovation
